questions.text: How should this local-source article handle exact CSI MasterFormat division claims?

options.text: Restore exact CSI divisions from memory
Defer exact CSI claims until a local CSI primary source is added
Treat CSI as a Philippine law

questions.rationale: The checked packet supports specifications generally, but not exact CSI MasterFormat structure.
questions.explanation: Confuses MasterFormat with cost data; MasterFormat is an organizational system, not a cost index. Completely unrelated; MasterFormat is an organizational system, not a paint brand. Confuses MasterFormat with building codes; MasterFormat is a specification organization system, not a safety standard. CSI MasterFormat is the Construction Specifications Institute standard system organizing trades into numbered divisions (01–48) and subsections, ensuring logical organization and industry standardization. CSI MasterFormat (50 divisions) is the standard specification organization system—ensures everyone can locate information consistently.

questions.text: What is a performance specification in the checked government-procurement context?

options.text: A specification stated by characteristics or performance requirements

questions.rationale: RA 9184 IRR supports specifications based on characteristics or performance requirements.
questions.explanation: False; performance specifications include clear acceptance standards and testing requirements. Incorrect scope; performance specifications are used on both public and private projects. False; performance specifications are common for results dependent on methodology (acoustic, thermal, water-tightness performance). Performance specifications define the desired outcome (e.g., water-tightness) and verification methods (testing standards) but allow contractors to choose materials and methods that achieve the result. Performance = 'define the result'—lets contractors innovate; requires clear acceptance criteria and testing procedures.

questions.text: Why is vague specification language risky?

options.text: It makes requirements harder to price, build, inspect, and interpret
It eliminates the need for drawings
It transfers all professional responsibility to the owner

questions.rationale: Specifications function as contract documents; unclear requirements create pricing, construction, and interpretation risk.

questions.text: What makes a specification professionally useful?

options.text: It is coordinated with drawings and states material, workmanship, performance, or installation requirements clearly

questions.rationale: The source-safe standard is coordinated, clear, contract-document language.

questions.text: When should specifications be updated during the design process?

options.text: As design moves from outline specifications in design development to technical specifications in contract documents

questions.rationale: UAP Standards place outline specifications in design development and technical specifications in contract documents.
questions.explanation: False; as design evolves from schematic to DD to CD, specifications require refinement. Dangerous; informal changes without notice create disputes and allow contractors to claim ambiguity. False; specifications can and should be updated through design phases to reflect design refinement. Design Development phase specifications may be preliminary and refined during detailed design; Construction Document specifications must be final and complete; any changes during construction must be issued through formal addenda or change orders. Update specs from DD to CD to finalize them; any changes during construction require formal addenda—informal changes create disputes.

questions.text: What is the architect’s risk if specifications are incomplete or poorly coordinated?

options.text: Conflicts, claims, defective work, pricing errors, and responsibility for unclear professional documents
No risk because specifications are decorative

questions.rationale: The checked sources tie specifications to contract documents and architect responsibility.

questions.text: What should happen when drawings and specifications conflict?

options.text: The issue should be submitted for written architect clarification or decision

questions.rationale: UAP Document 301 supports written clarification when drawings and specifications conflict or are obscure.

questions.text: What is a prescriptive specification safest understood to do?

options.text: State required materials, workmanship, or installation in coordinated contract-document language
State only a performance outcome and no method ever

questions.rationale: A prescriptive specification states requirements directly, but must remain coordinated with drawings and the contract documents.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of technical specifications?

options.text: To communicate enforceable requirements for materials, workmanship, performance, and construction quality alongside the drawings

questions.rationale: Specifications communicate contract requirements and support bidding, construction, inspection, and interpretation.
